narratives.Overview:
## Status

Confirmed by direct reproduction against the published v0.108.0 package. Both failures remain present on current `master`.

## Summary

Make direct-CLI and Task-runner read-only syntax unambiguous, and suppress recoverable Git probe stderr when session startup succeeds.

## Confirmed reproduction

From a valid generic consumer Git repository with `@deftai/directive` v0.108.0:

```text
$ deft session:start -- --read-only
session_start: unrecognized argument: --
# exit 2

$ deft session:start --read-only
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
Deft Directive active -- AGENTS.md loaded.
...
[deft scm] SCM ready: gh present, host-gh authenticated (shallow)
[deft] read-only session posture (alignment only; no ritual-state write)
# exit 0
```

## Root causes

### Syntax mismatch

- Generated instructions advertise direct `deft session:start -- --read-only`: [`commands.md:408-414`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/content/commands.md#L408-L414).
- The direct CLI parser accepts `--read-only` and sends a bare `--` to the generic unrecognized-argument branch: [`session-start.ts:105-114`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/cli/src/session-start.ts#L105-L114).
- The separator is appropriate for Task forwarding (`task session:start -- --read-only`), not currently for direct `deft` invocation.

### Contradictory Git stderr

- The managed-AGENTS framework-SHA probe runs `git rev-parse` against the resolved framework root: [`agents-md.ts:69-82`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts#L69-L82).
- In an installed package, that framework root need not be a Git checkout.
- The failure is intentionally recoverable (`unknown` SHA), but child-process stderr reaches the terminal before the exception is caught.

## Expected behavior

- Direct CLI documentation uses `deft session:start --read-only`.
- Task-runner documentation uses `task session:start -- --read-only` where the separator is needed for argument forwarding.
- A successful read-only session does not print a raw fatal line from a recoverable framework metadata probe.
- An actual final SCM/configuration failure remains visible and actionable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Choose and document the canonical direct-CLI syntax as `deft session:start --read-only`.
- [ ] Keep Task-runner separator examples explicit and distinct from direct CLI examples.
- [ ] Update every generated/template/managed instruction atomically.
- [ ] Add parser/entrypoint tests for direct CLI and Task forwarding forms.
- [ ] Capture recoverable framework-SHA probe stderr and return `unknown` silently.
- [ ] Preserve actionable stderr when the final command outcome genuinely fails.
- [ ] Add an installed-package regression fixture whose framework root is not a Git repository.
- [ ] Prove a successful invocation emits no contradictory `fatal: not a git repository` line.

## Related

No semantically matching open issue was found during title, body, comment, and symbol searches at filing time.

## Road not taken

I chose between two mechanisms for reconciling the two spellings: rewrite the instruction surface to the bare-flag form (what the issue proposes), or add the separator arm to the one parser that lacks it. ## Steelman of the rejected position

The strongest case for the issue's direction: `--` is genuinely meaningless to a direct binary invocation, `deft session:start --read-only` is the POSIX-canonical spelling, and the eighteen tolerant parsers are accumulated compensation for a documentation habit rather than a designed convention. On that reading, teaching one spelling shrinks the documented cross-product permanently and the proposed remedy is the honest cleanup, while adding a nineteenth tolerance entrenches the habit.

What would flip my verdict: a recorded decision that the `--` spelling in direct-`deft` documentation is a retiring error class, together with a scope that covers `-- --compact`, `-- --with-network`, and `-- --defer`, and that states what happens to the eighteen tolerant parsers and to the test at `verify-session-ritual.test.ts:40-42` that currently locks the opposite. Absent that record, the asymmetry between `session:start` and the `session:ready` that composes it is the defect, and it is one file.

## Verdict

The canonical direct spelling survives refutation: `deft session:start --read-only` is the right documented form, while Task needs its own forwarding separator. The clean-success requirement is also right. The design does not yet bind as written, though, because the framework-SHA remedy treats “not a checkout” only as a failing Git command. ## Findings

### 1. The SHA probe can silently stamp an unrelated ancestor repository

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence: at dispatch SHA `0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87`, [`platform/agents-md.ts:69-82`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts#L69-L82) runs `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` with `cwd=frameworkRoot` and trusts any successful stdout. In a controlled fixture, I initialized a Git repository, placed a non-repository `vendor/framework` directory beneath it, and passed that directory as `frameworkRoot`; `agentsRefreshPlan` returned the parent repository's 12-character HEAD. The installed Homebrew layout exhibits the same shape: the package directory is not a checkout, but Git walks upward to `/opt/homebrew`, so the probe can return Homebrew's HEAD rather than `unknown`. Capturing stderr cannot affect this path because Git exits successfully.

Concrete failure mode: a managed `sha=` marker can identify the package manager's or another enclosing repository's revision. Managed-section refresh and drift reporting then compare against false provenance while producing no warning—the silent result looks healthier than the noisy failure being fixed.

Disposition consequence: the current root-cause/acceptance contract is incomplete and cannot bind. A framework SHA should be eligible only when the resolved framework root is itself the Git top level; otherwise it should be `unknown`. The tree already contains both halves of a suitable mechanism: [`payloadIsOwnGitRoot`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/core/src/platform/resolve-version.ts#L85-L97) defines the root-equality semantics, and [`defaultGitRunner`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/core/src/session/git.ts#L28-L58) captures child stderr. Add a nested-under-unrelated-repository regression, not only a directory with no Git ancestor. The duplicate resolver in [`doctor/agents-md.ts:45-63`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/core/src/doctor/agents-md.ts#L45-L63) is silent but has the same boundary error, so fixing only the platform copy leaves divergent semantics.

### 2. Canonical documentation and parser tolerance are separate decisions

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: against the installed v0.109.0 entrypoint in a valid temporary consumer Git repository, direct `--read-only` exited 0 (and reproduced the raw Git fatal), while direct `-- --read-only` exited 2 with `unrecognized argument: --`. That confirms the issue's syntax premise. But adjacent direct parsers deliberately tolerate the sentinel: [`session-ready.ts:31-35`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/cli/src/session-ready.ts#L31-L35) and [`verify-session-ritual.ts:43-47`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/cli/src/verify-session-ritual.ts#L43-L47) skip bare `--`. Task forwarding is a third layer: [`tasks/session.yml:19-21`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/tasks/session.yml#L19-L21) injects Task's `CLI_ARGS` into the same handler.

Concrete failure mode: “canonical direct spelling has no separator” can be overread as “the direct parser must reject the separator,” even though those are different compatibility contracts and neighboring lifecycle verbs take the opposite position. Tests can then cement an accidental one-verb inconsistency or silently broaden the parser while claiming only a documentation correction.

Disposition consequence: keep the no-separator direct spelling as canonical, but record separately whether direct `session:start` intentionally rejects bare `--` or tolerates it as an undocumented compatibility form. The direct-entrypoint and Task-forwarding tests should assert that chosen boundary explicitly.

### 3. The authority surface and stderr assertion need end-to-end observability

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: the stale spelling is present in `content/commands.md`, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, and generated `AGENTS.md`, and is also required by `agents_md_session_start.test.ts` (two assertions) and `agents_entry_contract.test.ts` (one canonical marker). A targeted run of four relevant test files passed all 105 tests while still printing `fatal: not a git repository`; [`branch-coverage.test.ts:581-592`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0de4d5a29c0d4465fc339094f72f659d73dd6f87/packages/core/src/platform/branch-coverage.test.ts#L581-L592) checks only the returned `unknown`, not the child-process stderr visible to a user.

Concrete failure mode: source-level tests remain green while the real entrypoint emits contradictory diagnostics, or one generated instruction surface continues teaching agents the failing command. Because managed `AGENTS.md` is an authority-bearing prompt surface, a partial rewrite propagates the defect into future sessions even if the parser itself is correct. This is the relevant injection/authority lens; the proposed change does not otherwise alter identity, concurrency, worktrees, or shared state.

Disposition consequence: make the atomic rewrite observable in content-contract tests with distinct direct and Task spellings, regenerate the managed section from its template, and spawn both entrypoints in regression tests that assert exit status plus captured stdout and stderr. Monkey-patching `process.stderr.write` inside the process is insufficient for child stderr emitted by `execFileSync`.

## Road not taken and steelman

The tempting narrow fix is to add piped `stdio` to the one `execFileSync` call, or copy the doctor's `spawnSync` pattern. That is the strongest version of the current design: it is small, uses an existing pattern, and removes the reported fatal in the no-ancestor fixture. I reject it as sufficient because it preserves the successful ancestor lookup and the duplicated boundary-blind resolver. The blocking verdict flips when the contract adds own-Git-root semantics and the nested-ancestor case, while the two entrypoint tests demonstrate clean successful output.

## Protocol fit

The refutation charter fits the defensible canonical-syntax premise. I resolved the dispatch SHA, used no audit targets, and stopped thread input at inclusive comment `5501943027`; no later comment informed this pass.
